LESSON: CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: ARABIC
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.8: Conversational Skills

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Conversational Skills. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why are non-verbal cues key in communication?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify non- verbal cues used for effective communication
2. use appropriate non-verbal cues in oral presentations

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS
Subject: ARABIC · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Conversational Skills helps you succeed in ARABIC. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school and at home in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS
Study Conversational Skills like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Identify non- verbal cues used for effective communication

What this means
In this part you learn to identify non- verbal cues used for effective communication. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify non- verbal cues used for effective communication.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Explain “Conversational Skills” in your own words using one local example.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify non- verbal cues used for effective communication. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use appropriate non-verbal cues in oral presentations

What this means
In this part you learn to use appropriate non-verbal cues in oral presentations. You will use ideas from at school and at home in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use appropriate non-verbal cues in oral presentations.
2. Read, practise, then check using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Show one correct way to practise Conversational Skills.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use appropriate non-verbal cues in oral presentations. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Conversational Skills is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Explain “Conversational Skills” in your own words using one local example. (skill: identify non- verbal cues used for effective communication)

Example 2: Show one correct way to practise Conversational Skills. (skill: use appropriate non-verbal cues in oral presentations)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Conversational Skills to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify non- verbal cues used for effective communication.
3. Practise this skill: use appropriate non-verbal cues in oral presentations.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Conversational Skills from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Conversational Skills: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Conversational Skills?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why are non-verbal cues key in communication?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Conversational Skills means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify non- verbal cues used for effective communication.
5. Be able to: use appropriate non-verbal cues in oral presentations.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
